title.narrative: Inclusive Livestock Development for Smallholder Farmers

description.narrative:
INCLUDE has four long-term outcomes:
1. Increased smallholder farmers' productivity: 90,000 farmers benefit from increased productivity.
2. Sustainable smallholder farmers' land use: Manage 37,500 acres for improved productivity.
3. Improved market access for smallholder farmers: 90,000 farmers gain better market access.
4. Improved access to nutritious food: **300,000 **schoolchildren benefit from milk or milk-based foods.
The geographical Area: Busoga, Rwenzori, Greater Ankole and Kigezi sub-regions of Uganda.
The project has three pathways:
1. Sustainable Production: This integrated crop-livestock system improves soil fertility, diversifies smallholder farmer enterprises, and enhances the production and quality of livestock products.
2. Inclusive Livestock Markets: INCLUDE will be smallholder farmer-led and market-oriented and strengthen linkages between smallholder farmers and market actors for inputs, outputs, and financial services, enhancing the capacity and voice of smallholder farmers, cooperatives, and village-based marketing groups. It will also develop and strengthen private sector local market actors and link them with interested international (Dutch) companies to ensure that SHFs are an essential market segment with growth potential for their businesses.
3. School Milk Programme and Milk Market: INCLUDE will raise community awareness and participation in the school milk programme, boosting smallholder farmer milk sales to schools and collection centres.
INCLUDE

The Inclusive Livestock Development for Smallholder Farmers (INCLUDE) Project is a five-year initiative from April 2024 to March 2029. Implemented by SNV and funded by the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, the project aims to improve the livelihoods and resilience of smallholder farmers in Uganda. INCLUDE will empower 75,000 smallholder farmers (SHFs) and have improved market access for 90,000 SHFs in Kigezi, Greater Ankole, Rwenzori, and Busoga to achieve resilient livelihoods and a living income through sustainable, high-frequency, and livestock-based practices. The project’s vision is to promote equitable, sustainable, and resilient livelihoods for smallholder farmers, as well as reduce productivity loss and adaptation to climate shocks and market failure.
The project uses a farming systems approach integrating livestock (dairy cattle, sheep, goats, poultry, and piggery) and crops, with livestock as the entry point.
The PIP (Participatory Integrated Planning) approach, which transforms small-scale subsistence farms into productive, sustainable farms, guides INCLUDE farmers’ participation. PIP involves creating a visionary Integrated Farm Plan drawn by all family members and a concrete action plan to achieve that vision based on intrinsic motivation.
The core of PIP is changing farmers’ mindsets through collective action. The project will enhance smallholder resilience, productivity, and income, support access to markets and market development, the school milk programme, and aid in developing inclusive, responsive livestock policies.

title.narrative: Project photo
Increased SHF living income & resilient livestock-based livelihoods for smallholder farmers in Kigezi, Greater Ankole, Rwenzori, and Busoga (ABCD)
Number of SHF who progressively realize a living income (B&D)

description.narrative:
**Definition:** A living income is the income earned by SHF with which they are able to meet their basic needs without external support. The basic needs in this case include health care, education, clothing, housing, food and water.
**Measurement:** This is a count of SHFs who raise their income towards a living income for their household. Income is not precisely measured by this indicator so there is no application of a monetary threshold to what counts as a living income.

title.narrative: Number of SHF households whose livelihoods became more resilient to shocks (agency, buffer, connectivity, diversity)

description.narrative:
**Definition:** Resilience of SHF Livelihoods is defined as the capacity to resist, recover from, and/or adjust to disruptions and stresses that (may) adversely affect their livelihoods.
**Measurement:** This is a count of all SHF households with an increased capacity to maintain, recover or adjust their livelihood base – with a view to maintaining their engagement in food production – when faced with shocks or stresses. The shocks and stressess include but not limited to adverse weather, disease, price fluctuations, and soil infertility.
Measurement of resilience is based on the SNV ABCD resilience framework which inludes measurement of the 4 ABCD domains over time as well as a qualitative assessment of changes in resilience of SHF from their own perspectives.

title.narrative: Increased SHF adoption of integrated climate-sensitive practices incl. integration of livestock into farming systems (D)
Number of SHF households adopting integrated climate-sensitive practices

description.narrative:
Definition: Adoption of Integrated Climate-sensitive agriculture practices are defined as the application of multiple components of the farming system, including crops, livestock, soil, water, and other resources, that are designed to adapt to or mitigate the impacts of climate change in a cohesive manner.
This indicator measures the number of targeted SHF households who have resolved to and are practicing improved/better integrated climate sensitive farming practices for a period of two (2) or more agricultural seasons and foresee themselves continuing with the practice in the coming agriculture seasons (adoption). Adoption means that the practice has been used for 2 or more consecutive agriculture seasons and that there is intention for continued practice in the future. Integrated climate sensitive practices in this case will be interpreted as climate sensitive system or mechanical equipment or agriculture approach, such as advanced marketing.
Measurement: This is a count of SHF households that engage or adopt/apply multiple (two or more integrated climate sensitive practices) component of farming systems that are designed to adapt to and mitigate the impacts of climate change for two consecutive agriculture seasons with intention of continuity in the future.
The calculation is as follows; number of sampled targeted SHF households adopting any of the Climate-sensitive agriculture practices as defined above divided by the total number of surveyed targeted SHF households multiplied by 117,775 (total reach of SHF households through climate-sensitive practices).
These practices may include; advanced livestock production, aggregation, value-addition, agro-processing, agro-forestry, livestock-crop rotation, manure management, diversification of breeds, zero-grazing with improved fodder, new breeds, solar technologies, advanced marketing of livestock products, etc.

title.narrative: Intermediate outcome 3: Improved SHF agricultural practices
Number of SHF households applying at least three good agricultural practices

description.narrative:
Definition: Improved agricultural practices are farming methods and techniques that not only facilitate efficient food production, but also prevent losses of land and water, safeguard natural resources, and promote biodiversity e.g timely planting, integrated pest management, seeds/breeds selection, post harvest handling, soil and water conservation, etc
Measurement: A count of the number of SHF households that apply any 3 improved/good agricultural practices from the practices recommended by FAO.

title.narrative: Improved production & quality of SHF livestock products
Number of SHF households with improved quality of livestock & related products

description.narrative:
Definition: Improved quality refers to enhancements in the attributes or characteristics of livestock and their products. These improvements can include better health, productivity, and marketability.
Measurement: This is a count of SHF households that identify enhancements in the attributes or characteristics of their livestock and the associated products

title.narrative: Increased SHF access to finance (B&C)
Number of SHFs receiving loan through SACCOs (C)

description.narrative: This is a count of the number of SHF stating having received a loan from financial services providers.

title.narrative: Volume of loans issued to SHFs by SACCOs

description.narrative: This is the total amount of the dairy loan fund (in UGX) provided to SHFs through support services providers/financial institutions (SACCOs).

title.narrative: Improved SHF participation, voice, decision making and adaptive capacity (A)
Number of communities with PIP and action plan (A)

description.narrative:
A count of the number of communities with PIP and action plan.
A PIP Community is composed of averagely 250 to 500 SHF households who are participating in PIP training with the intention of developing community vision.
An action plan states planned activities, how, when the planned activities will be achieved with what resources.

title.narrative: Number of PIP Innovators capacitated and transferring knowledge on integrated farming practices to SHF households

description.narrative: A count of number of PIP Innovators (lead farmers) and extension workers with enhanced capacity transferring knowledge and skills gained on integrated farming practices to SHF households in their community.

title.narrative: Number of SHF households with household visions and action plan (A)

description.narrative: A count of the number of SHF households that developed household level action plan linked to a household vision.

title.narrative: Long-term outcome 1: Sustainably increased SHF production (D)
Number of acres of agricultural land under productive and sustainable agriculture

description.narrative:
**Definition:** productive and sustainable agriculture is defined as agriculture that yields sufficient quantities of crops or livestock products and the associated practices that maintain or enhance the long-term health of the land and environment. Key aspects of productive agriculture here include, high crop yields, efficient use of inputs, and effective management of livestock. while the aspects of sustainable agriculture include practices that improve soil health, conserve water, reduce erosion, promote biodiversity, and minimize pollution and waste.
**Measurement**: This is the sum of acres that are under agricultural use that yield sufficient yields of crops and livestock products without compromising soil health, conserve water and promote biodiversity among others

title.narrative: Improved SHF participation, voice, decision making and adaptive capacity (A)
Number of SHF households who participate in PIP sessions that state inclusive decisions in the implementation of action plans for their enterprises

description.narrative:
A count of number of SHF households where there is joint household decisions as a result of participation in PIP
Joint household decisions refers to all members of the household taking part in decision making pertaining their livelihoods. Decisions could be on purchasing inputs, sale of produce, when where and what to plant, etc.

title.narrative: Contribution to improved access to nutritious food
Number of school-going children consuming milk or milk-based foods

description.narrative:
A count of number of children from schools enrolled on school feeding consuming milk or milk-based foods through routine data collection activites. It is measured through routine data collection activities, including reports from schools, monitoring visits, and periodic surveys.
The term milk or milk-based foods refers to either yogurt, cheese, fresh milk or other dairy products included in school feeding programs. This will assess the number of students benefiting nutritionally from the inclusion of dairy products in the school feeding.

title.narrative: Change of perceptions of SHF parents towards their children consuming milk and milk-based products at school

description.narrative: Measures level of changes in perceptions among SHF parents of school-going children about the value of their children consuming milk and milk-based foods at school. Assess the number of parents of school-going children of targeted schools participating in the SMP showcasing positive changes in their perceptions towards the SMP.

title.narrative: Increased transactions between SHF and input suppliers, buyers & support service providers in agricultural markets (C)
Number of market actors (input/output suppliers, buyers, support service providers) offering different services to smallholder farmers in agricultural markets

description.narrative:
A count of the number of market actors (input/output suppliers, buyers, support service providers) that are offering tailored services & products to SHFs in the agricultural markets.
Measurement: Count the number of market actors (input/output suppliers, buyers, and support service providers) that are offering tailored products & services to SHFs with linkages due to connectivity to suppliers and off-takers in the markets. This will be conducted through network analysis of market actors.

title.narrative: Increased awareness and participation of local community (parents, teachers, leaders) in school milk programme
Number of schools participating in school milk program

description.narrative: A count of the number of participating schools in the school milk program (SMP).

title.narrative: Increased (off farm) employment opportunities in livestock value chain (D)
Number of people gaining decent off-farm (self) employment

description.narrative:
Definition: Decent off-farm employment is defined as a job that is not agricultural related, offers dignity, comensurate compensation, and stability.
Measurement: This is a count of all persons that gain such employment directly or indirectly as a result of the project interventions

title.narrative: Increased types of appropriate financial products and services developed and used by SHF.
Number of SHFs having meaningful access to appropriate financial products and services for use in their livestock value chain

description.narrative:
Definition:
A count of the number of SHF households that report having meaningful access to appropriate types of financial products and services for use in their livestock value chain.
Meaningful access means financial products and services that are available within the required timeframe, sufficient value (amount), meet the specific needs of livestock SHF household, known by SHFs potentially accessing the products and services, physically (easy reach) and financially accessible, and culturally relevant & socially acceptable.

title.narrative: Increased capacity & voice of SHF, farmer groups, cooperatives & value chain actors including village-based marketing (A&C)
Number of farmer groups, cooperatives, and village-based marketing groups formed/strengthened (A&C)

description.narrative:
Definition:
A count of the number of groups supported by the project that are strengthened in terms of capacity and voice.
Capacity refers to a combination of all the strengths and resources available within a community or society that may include physical, institutional, social or economic means as well as skilled personnel or collective attributes.

title.narrative: Increased awareness and recognition of SHF benefits & opportunities
Number of SHFs with demonstrable awareness on benefits and opportunities in the livestock sector

description.narrative:
Definition:
Benefits include tangible and intangible advantages that SHFs, and communities gain from livestock activities e.g., increased income, environmental and social gains derived from sustainable livestock practices.
Opportunities include potential areas for growth, innovation e.g., expansion into new markets, value addition, diversified practices, better technologies, better management practices, and untapped potential that can enhance productivity, profitability, and sustainability within the livestock value chain.
Measurement: A count of the number of smallholder farmers who demonstrate an increased understanding of the benefits and opportunities of integrated livestock farming system.

title.narrative: Improved & diversified SHF enterprise mix (crop-livestock) (D)
Number of SHF households with at least three crop and livestock diversification

description.narrative:
Definition:
This indicator measures the number of SHF households that have diversified their production systems by cultivating a combination of at least three livestock-crop types/species. Diversification here implies the combination of various crops and livestock to increase resilience and farm incomes. Crops species may include maize, beans, soy beans, banana, etc. Livestock types may include dairy cows/cattle, goats, sheep, rabbits, poultry, etc.
Measurement:
A count of the number of SHF households meeting the three-enterprise threshold. A SHF household cultivating a minimum of two different crop species plus raising a minimum of one livestock type or atleast two livestock types (e.g., cattle, goats, sheep, poultry, piggery) and at least one crop type. Surveys will be employed to collect data on the types of crops and livestock types SHF households are managing in the past 12 months. Assess whether diversification was intentional and sustainable through interviews and/or FGDs (e.g., market access, incomes, climate events, etc).

title.narrative: Improved more inclusive access for SHF to input and output markets
Number of SHFs getting fair prices for their agricultural products

description.narrative:
Definition:
This indicator measures the number of SHFs who receive fair prices for their agricultural products when selling to output markets. "Fair prices" are defined as prices that reflect the true value of the products based on market demand, quality. It assesses whether SHFs are receiving prices that allow them to cover their production costs, achieve a reasonable profit, and support the sustainability of their farming system. Fair prices are equitable across different groups of SHFs and ensure that both women, youth, men and marginalised groups are not disproportionately disadvantaged by market forces or unfair trading practices. It measures whether SHFs are able to engage in markets on equal terms with larger or more influential market players.
Measurement:
Use sample survey to estimate the number of SHFs receiving prices that are equal to or above market value and that provide a profit margin that supports reinvestment in the farm and improves the SHF’s livelihood. Compare SHFs' selling prices to market prices reported in the same region for similar products. Assess whether SHFs are engaged in transparent and equitable transactions with buyers (e.g., cooperatives, middlemen, or direct market access). Fair prices often depend on SHFs' ability to negotiate and access higher-paying buyers. Interview SHFs to assess their satisfaction with prices, their perceptions of market fairness, and any challenges they face in negotiating or accessing better prices.

title.narrative: Number of SHFs using relevant inputs

description.narrative:
Definition:
This indicator tracks the number of SHFs who are consistently using relevant inputs for their farming operations. Relevant inputs refer to any agricultural resources, products or services that directly enhance SHF livestock and crop productivity, sustainability, profitability, resilience to environmental stresses, or resource efficiency. Examples include seeds, fertilizers, pesticides, animal feed, veterinary services, equipment, and other farming tools. The relevance of these inputs is context-dependent, determined by local crop/livestock needs, environmental conditions, and market demand.
It measures access to and use of inputs that are essential for SHFs. It also provides insight into the inclusivity of input markets. The relevance of inputs depends on local conditions, farming practices, market demands, and the specific needs of the SHFs. Inputs must be adapted to support both the crop and livestock components of the SHF farming system.
Measurement:
Use surveys to assess the types of inputs SHFs are using in their farms, frequency of use, and whether the inputs were accessed from formal or informal markets. Verify the presence of inputs on SHF farms, such as fertilizers, seeds, or livestock feeds, and whether these inputs are appropriate for the farming context. Relevancy of inputs means it meets their specific needs based on their contexts. SHFs must report using at least one input that is critical for their crop or livestock operations during the growing season. Inputs must be applied according to recommended practices (e.g., correct amount of fertilizers). Using sample surveys, estimate the number of SHFs using relevant inputs.

title.narrative: More stable and sustainable prices for SHF realised
Number of SHF households that received stable and sustainable prices for their products across seasons

description.narrative:
Definitions:
Stable prices exhibit minimal fluctuations across agricultural seasons and ensures that SHF households receives predictable incomes from their products e.g., milk, meat, etc regardless of seasonal variations in demand or supply. This enables SHF households to cover basic operational costs (feed, veterinary care, etc.) without experiencing significant financial strain due to sudden drops in market prices.
Sustainable prices cover not only the cost of production but also provide enough profit to maintain and improve the SHF household's livelihood over time (1 year or more). These prices should allow for re-investment in the farm (e.g., buying better livestock breeds, improving farm infrastructure, water technologies, improved forage production, reducing the environmental footprint of the farm, etc) while maintaining environmental and economic viability.
This may include SHF household signing contract with a stable buyer e.g VMMGs having contracts with off-takers to supply their milk products for a year or more.
Measurement: Count the number of SHF households linked to relevant market actors (e.g off-takers) who received stable or sustainable prices for their products across two agricultural seasons or more.

title.narrative: Output 1: Improved soil fertility for SHF
Number of SHF households that achieved improved soil fertility due to applying at least three soil fertility specific ISL practices

description.narrative: Measurement: A count of the number of SHF households that report increased soil fertility upon applying soil fertility specific practices that have been supported through the project via training, extension, and/or private sector service provider support.

title.narrative: Long-term outcome 2: Increased SHF income realised from livestock + crops (B)
Number of SHFs benefiting from increased farm income

description.narrative:
This indicator measures the number of people benefitting from an increase in income at farm level as a result of project activities.
Measurement: Use sampled household survey to collect data on relevant income generating activities at farm level. Triangulate survey data with data from farmers that keep records on yield, inputs, prices and costs.
The change in income is measured at farm household level with smallholder farm households participating in the project. Change in income is estimated through the collection and triangulation of proxy data.
For Livestock: Collect data on income generated from sales of animals and or animal produce, and production costs. The survey should focus on the last season. Collect this data at approximately the same time each year for data to be comparable year on year.
For Crops: Collect data on production volumes (harvested whether sold or for home consumption), farm gate prices received for sold crops, and input costs (variable costs) e.g costs for land preparation, land rent, seed, agro-chemicals, fuel, and hired labour. Consider the lowest price as a conservative estimate where there are multiple farmgate prices over the selling season.
A standardised survey is available to collect data on farm income. Survey data to be triangulated with data from farmers that keep books on yield, inputs, prices and costs.

title.narrative: Increased SHF knowledge application of integrated farming methods
Number of SHFs trained in integrated farming methods who consistently applied at least three of the methods on their plots/farms across multiple seasons

description.narrative: This indicator will measure the number of smallholder farmers (SHFs) trained in integrated farming methods who consistently applied at least three of the integrated farming methods (e.g., use of organic manure, crop-livestock integration, agroforestry, mulching, terracing) on their plots/farms across multiple seasons (for at least two consecutive seasons). "Consistent application” means that the integrated farming methods has been applied for at least two consecutive agriculture seasons during a given year and the SHF has intention of continuation of application in future.

title.narrative: Increased SHF & farmer group sales of milk to schools & rural milk off-takers/collection centres
Annual milk sales volume from SHF & farmer groups to schools or via collective bulking/marketing

description.narrative: This is the sum of the volume of milk sold by SHF households to schools participating in the SMP directly or indirectly via Village Milk Marketing Groups, or collective bulking of milk through off-takers.
